arxiv-2504-18447.title: Iterative Event-based Motion Segmentation by Variational Contrast Maximization
arxiv-2504-18447.creator: Ryo Yamaki, Shintaro Shiba, Guillermo Gallego, Yoshimitsu Aoki
arxiv-2504-18447.description: Abstract Event cameras provide rich signals that are suitable for motion estimation since they respond to changes in the scene. arxiv-2512-16116.title: Rota-Baxter operators on braces, post-braces and the Yang-Baxter equation
arxiv-2512-16116.creator: Li Guo, Yan Jiang, Yunhe Sheng, You Wang
arxiv-2512-16116.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Li Guo, Yan Jiang, Yunhe Sheng, You Wang. Combining the notions of braces and relative Rota-Baxter operators on groups in connection with the Yang-Baxter equation and a factorization theorem of Lie groups from integrable systems, relative Rota-Baxter operators on braces and post-braces are introduced. A relative Rota-Baxter operator on a brace naturally induces a post-brace, and conversely, every post-brace determines a relative Rota-Baxter operator on its sub-adjacent brace. Furthermore, a post-brace yields two Drinfel’d-isomorphic solutions to the Yang-Baxter equation.

pmc-11484020.title: The role of interferon signaling in neurodegeneration and neuropsychiatric disorders
pmc-11484020.creator: Daniel W. Sirkis, Alexis P. Oddi, Caroline Jonson, Luke W. Bonham, Phuong T. Hoang, Jennifer S. Yokoyama
pmc-11484020.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Recent advances in transcriptomics research have uncovered heightened interferon (IFN) responses in neurodegenerative diseases including Alzheimer’s disease, primary tauopathy, Parkinson’s disease, TDP-43 proteinopathy, and related mouse models. Augmented IFN signaling is now relatively well established for microglia in these contexts, but emerging work has highlighted a novel role for IFN-responsive T cells in the brain and peripheral blood in some types of neurodegeneration.

pmc-11598466.description: Introducing dynamic ester bonds into epoxy–anhydride resins enhances the reprocessability of the crosslinked network, facilitated by various types of transesterification catalysts. Here, we propose to solve such problems by incorporating a liquid-state, thermally stable transesterification catalyst into epoxy resins.

pmc-11641098.title: c-Myc and FOXO3a—The Everlasting Decision Between Neural Regeneration and Degeneration
pmc-11641098.creator: Andrey M. Khaitin, Valeria V. Guzenko, Stanislav S. Bachurin, Svetlana V. Demyanenko
pmc-11641098.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). The transcription factors c-Myc and FoxO3a play significant roles in neurodegenerative processes, yet their interaction in neurological disorders remains largely unexplored. In contrast, much of the available information about their relationship comes from cancer research. While it is well-established that FoxO3a inhibits c-Myc activity, this interaction represents only a basic understanding of a far more complex dynamic, which includes exceptions under specific conditions and the involvement of additional regulatory factors.

pmc-13296863.title: Marine Invertebrate-Inspired Thermal Management: Functional Materials, Structural Architectures, and Integrated Systems
pmc-13296863.creator: Hoejin Jung, Inhye Shin, Sunwoo Kim, Sieun Jung, Jaeik Kim, Won-gyu Bae
pmc-13296863.description: Marine invertebrates exhibit diverse thermoregulatory capabilities enabled by hierarchical architectures, porous skeletal frameworks, and adaptive interfaces. This review surveys marine-invertebrate-inspired thermal management from an engineering perspective and synthesizes biological structure–function relationships into transferable design concepts.
